text:
歡迎來到政治大學英語教學碩士在職專班 / Welcome to ETMA, NCCU

本專班成立於民國88年，成立目的為配合教育部『建立高等教育回流體系實施案』，以落實終身教育的理念，並培養和訓練在職進修者的專業知識與技能。

發展重點在於提昇在職教師英語教學的品質，以符合當前國小、國中、高中各級教學目標的需求，其中包括教學課程規劃、教材內容之選擇、編纂和教學方法之研討改進，並加強在職教師認識『國際化政策』和『教學方針』的互動關係，培養在職教師結合科技新知與教學之能力，如推廣多媒體語言教學，以配合時代潮流。

The Master of Arts in English Teaching (ETMA) Program was established in 1999 to promote continuous learning and enhance the professional knowledge and skills of educators under the auspices of the “Implementation of Higher Education Extension Program” as set up by the Ministry of Education.

title: aboutetma.html
text:
英語教學碩士在職專班簡介

Introduction to the Master of Arts in English Teaching Program

 

本專班成立於民國88年，成立目的為配合教育部『建立高等教育回流體系實施案』，以落實終身教育的理念，並培養和訓練在職進修者的專業知識與技能。

The Master of Arts in English Teaching (ETMA) Program was established in 1999 to promote continuous learning and enhance the professional knowledge and skills of educators under the auspices of the "Implementation of Higher Education Extension Program" as set up by the Ministry of Education.

 

一、發展方向與重點 / Development Trend and Main Features ：

提昇在職教師英語教學的品質，以符合當前國小、國中、高中各級教學目標的需求，其中包括教學課程規劃、教材內容之選擇、編纂和教學方法之研討改進。

加強在職教師認識『國際化政策』和『教學方針』的互動關係。

培養在職教師結合科技新知與教學之能力，如推廣多媒體語言教學，以配合時代潮流。

  

To enhance the quality of English teaching among educators so that they will be better able to meet the individual needs of students in elementary school and high schools through lesson planning, selection of course contents, assessment and improvement of teaching strategies.

To help educators gain a better understanding of the interaction between “Internationalization Policies” and “Teaching Principles.”

To integrate technology into education through, for example, extending multimedia language teaching to follow the contemporary educational trends.

 

二、畢業學分 / Units Required for Graduation：

最低畢業學分共27學分，含必修「英語教學研究方法」3學分、「英語教學教材教法研究」3學分及「論文指導」3學分，其中「論文指導」為「碩士論文」先修課程。（適用於110學年度（含）後入學學生，108學年度以前入學學生最低畢業學分為36學分）

A total of 27 units is required for graduation, including two 3-unit required courses, “EFL Research Methods,” “Research Paper Writing”, and "Thesis Writing." 18 units of elective courses. Among them, the 3-unit “Thesis Writing” is a pre-requisite course for writing the thesis.

 

三、修業年限 / Length of Program：三至五年 / 3-5 years。

 

四、上課時間 / Class Schedule：

每年七月及八月(暑假期間) / July and August of each year (during summer vacation)

 

五、論文及口試 / Thesis and Oral Examination：

須修滿18學分，始得修習「論文指導」，且於修習此課程時，提出論文計畫書審查之申請 (110學年度後入學學生適用，108學年度以前入學學生須修滿24學分)。

論文考試申請時須通過論文計畫書審查，且完成論文。

論文須依照碩士在職專班之「碩士論文格式」，以英文撰寫。

論文考試時間為申請手續完成後三至六週舉行。

論文考試通過後，應於離校前繳交論文平裝兩冊至本碩士班，精裝兩冊至圖書館。

 

 

Students are required to complete a minimum of 24 units prior to taking “Thesis Writing”. A thesis proposal must be presented during enrollment for the course

The thesis proposal must be approved and the thesis must be completed prior to applying for the oral defense.

The thesis should be written in English, according to the standard thesis format as set out by the ETMA Program.

The thesis oral defense has to be held from 3 to 6 weeks after submission of the application.

After successful completion of the thesis oral defense, students should submit 2 copies of their thesis to the ETMA Program Office and three copies to the library before applying for leaving school.

 

 

六、學雜費及學分費 / Registration Fees and Credit Fees：

學雜費：准用本校公告之外語學院碩士班學基費收費標準

學分費：每學分4,500元。（未來將視狀況調整學費）

 

Registration fee is based on the standard of the Master Programs in College of Foreign Languages. Tuition is NT$4,500 per unit. (Fees are subject to change)

明德國中英語教師（女）

帶著慘綠少年的輕狂而來，才知自己的不學無術！師長們在談笑中即能傾囊相授打開知識之窗的門道，我才驚覺：聽力訓練不光是放卡帶就有效；一天唸兩百頁原文書的策略和技巧；影響語言學習的因素及迷思；寫作訓練的滴水穿石過程。而要經過寒澈骨的論文更是訓練獨立思考作學問的精髓！

這是兌變，在焚膏繼晷後。感謝每一位犧牲暑假的教授及助教！

基隆國中英語老師（男）

能再重溫學生生活，實在是一件令人愉悅的事，在教與學互相印證的前提下，在政大唸書實在是令人心曠神怡（當然，考試與交報告的壓力除外…）

內湖高中英語教師（女）

感謝政大開辦ETMA， 使我度過三個充實又愉快的暑假，功課壓力雖難免，但老師們都很nice又understanding，林老師的高級寫作，莫老師的字彙學，許老師的新聞英語與彭老師的新聞聽力訓練都是一級棒的，如果你來政大可千萬不能錯過喔！

華僑高中英語教師(女，已畢業)

拿到學位證書時，我的心是激動與感恩的。

ETMA的課程設計很精彩，雖然不能修到每位老師的課，但在ETMA四年的學習，開拓了我的教學視野，豐富了我的教學內涵。(也增加不少薪水)

Da Chi Senior High School: 

ETMA programs inspire me a lot not only in teaching but also in exchanging wonderful experiences with others. I really appreciate the time with all the prestigious and thoughtful teachers. I also cherish the time when we learned, discussed, even suffered, or tortured together.

title: facilities.html
text:
html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd"

為充分配合教學與研究需求，並避免資源浪費，本系乃成立圖書小組及設備小組，委請學有專長之教師擔任委員，負責規劃圖書、電腦及視聽器材之管理及增購事宜。與本系相關之圖書及視聽器材大多集中設置於本校中正圖書館、社會科學資料中心、語言視聽教育中心及電算中心，但為教學與研究方便，本系另自設有圖書室、視聽室、器材室、電腦室、會議室，及口譯教室等。

To satisfy the needs of teaching and research and to avoid waste, the department established the library and the equipment committees. These two committees are responsible for purchase and management of books, computers, and AV equipment. Most books and AV equipment are in the main library, the Social Sciences Data Center, the Language and Audio-visual Education Center, or the Computer Center. To assist those preparing for classes or conducting research, however, the department has its own library, AV Viewing Rooms, equipment room, computer room, meeting room and interpretation room.

 

圖書室 / Department Library：

現收藏英美文學、語言學及英語教學之圖書約壹萬餘冊、各式工具書百餘種、期刊十餘種。並設有電腦四台，以利上網蒐集資料。圖書室在圖書小組老師之指導下，由學生自行管理。

The library has a collection of more than ten thousand books representing English and American Literature, Linguistics and TESL, hundreds of reference books, and subscriptions to more than ten periodicals. The library is also equipped with four computers to facilitate information seeking on the Internet. Students manage the library under the direction of faculty members.

 

視聽室 / AV Viewing Room：

本系現有視聽室兩間----視聽室(I)及視聽室(II)，各可容納四十一名學生及二十九名學生。

視聽室(I)內設置：白板、電動螢幕一個、擴音喇叭四支，數位影碟機、錄放影機、擴大機各一台，及活動視聽機櫃一座(內含電視、數位影碟機、及錄放影機各一部)。

視聽室(II)內設置：白板、投影機、碟影機、字幕機、數位影碟機各一部，及電視機、錄放影機各二部。

The department has two AV Viewing Rooms-AV Viewing Room I seats 41 and AV Viewing Room II seats 29.

AV Viewing Room I is equipped with one white board, one built-in screen, four speakers, one DCD player, one VHS player, one amplifier and one portable cabinet for AV machines (including one TV, one DVD player and one VHS player.)

AV Viewing Room II is equipped with one white board, one projector, one VCD player, one closed caption decoder, one DVD player, two TVs and two VHS players.

 

器材室 / Equipment room：

存放磁帶消磁機、相機、實物投影機、手提單槍投影機、手提實物投影機、筆記型電腦、護貝機、翻譯機(transcriber)、幻燈片看片箱、活動視聽機櫃(內含電視機、錄放影機、及數位影碟機各一部)、電視、數位攝影機、教材提示機、數位錄音棒、快速拷貝機、幻燈機、投影機、腳架、攝影機、麥克風、小蜜蜂、錄音機十餘台、及各類教學用之錄音帶 、錄影帶、投影片等數百種，供教師借用，以輔助教學。

Used for storage of magnetic tape degaussers, cameras, portable visualizers, portable LCD projectors, notebooks, laminators, transcribers, slide-viewing machine, movable cabinet for AV machines (including one TV, one DVD player and one VHS player.), TVs, DV cameras, direct projectors, digital voice recorders, dubbing machines, slide projectors, overhead projectors, stands, cameras, microphone, tape recorders and hundreds of tape, video tape and slides for teaching.

 

電腦室 / Computer room：

本系設有電腦室一間，共存放九部個人電腦、噴墨印表機三部、及雷射印表機一部。

The department owns a computer room in which there are nine PCs, three ink jet printers and one laser printer.

 

會議室 / Meeting room：

本系設有小型會議室一間，約可容納二十五人。

One meeting room which seats 25.

 

口譯教室 / Interpretation room：

八十二學年經「教育部人文社會科學教育改進計畫」之經費補助而成立，位於語視中心二樓。內有多項視聽器材及同步翻譯之精密儀器，可容納約二十人。內含翻譯系統主控機、翻譯機、語言教學主控機、錄放音機、實物投影機、電視機、影碟機、影碟機用字幕機、攝影機及錄放影機等設備，並有電腦八部。

Subsidized by the Humanities and Social Science Education Improvement Program of the Ministry of Education, the interpretation room was constructed and is located on the second floor of Language and Audio-Visual Education Center. It is equipped with many items of AV and simultaneous interpretation equipment and it seats 20 people. Equipment includes translation primary console, transcribers, language teaching primary console, tape recorders, visualizer, TV set, VCD players, DVD decoder, cameras and VHS players and eight computers.

 (1) 加強教師語文能力； (2) 增進教師教學及解決教學困難問題之技巧；(3) 發展教學研究之能力。

2. 修滿18學分後，始得修習「論文指導」，於修習該課程時需提出論文/專業實務報告計劃書審查之申請。

3. 抵免學分上限為六學分，必修科目不得抵免，抵免科目成績須達八十五分以上，並需經過本專班課程委員會審定。

text:
英語教學碩士在職專班招生規定

Admission Requirements for Master of Arts in English Teaching

 

一、招生對象 / Prospective Students：

在職英語教師或從事英語教學相關職業人士並累計年資滿一年以上。年資以任職日起計，算至報考當年7月31日止。

In-service English teachers or in-service educators with at least one year of practical experience related to English teaching

Years of service are calculated from the date of employment to the July 31st of the application year.

 

二、招生名額 / Admission Quota：20名 / 20 applicants

 

三、簡章發售及報名 / Date for Application and Test Registration：

請參照本校招生簡章規定。

See the school's Admission brochure for reference

 

四、考試日期 / Test Date：

請參照本校招生簡章規定。

See the school's Admission brochure for reference

 

五、考試項目及成績計算 / Subjects Tested and Method of Calculating Score

筆試（50%）：英語教學理論與實務、英文能力測驗與寫作

口試（30%）：以英語進行，每位考生大約10分鐘口試時間

書面審查（20%）：教學經歷、英語教學經歷、英語進修經歷、進修計畫、其他相關資料

 

1. Written examination 50%

English Proticiency and Writing

The Theory and Practice of English Teaching

2. Oral examination (conducted in English) 30%

3. Evaluation of Application Documents 20%

Teaching Experience Evaluation Form

Proofs of English teaching experience

Proofs of advanced study in English

3 pages of study plan (written in English)

Other supporting documents related to English teaching or research

 

六、其他規定事項

◎報名時應另繳交資料：

[教學經歷審核表](https://drive.google.com/file/d/13azGZ7yhFY7eliSK9Rar0Xe3eRbwIDoW/view?usp=sharing)

相關文件：

(1)英語教學經歷相關證明影本。

(2)英語進修經歷相關證明影本。

(3)三頁之進修計畫（含英語教學心得及未來研究方向，以英文撰寫）。

(4) 其他有利申請之英語教學╱研究資料影本。

◎本專班錄取考生採通訊報到方式辦理，報到時間另行公告。

◎收費標準（108年度）

學雜費：準用本校公告之外語學院碩士班學基費收費標準。

學分費：每學分4,500元。

◎考生經考試錄取註冊入學後，其修課及畢業相關規定，請詳見本專班網頁。

※詳細口試時間及地點，於口試前公布於本專班網站。

title: 415-master-of-arts-in-english-teaching-etma-q-a.html
text:
英語教學碩士在職專班 (ETMA) Q＆A

Master of Arts in English Teaching (ETMA) Q&A

109.11.13

 

Ｑ：「英語教學碩士在職專班」上課時間為何? / When are ETMA classes held?

Ａ：暑假上課，共七週半。時間為7月及8月週(一)至(四)上下午。每一科目上課15次（54小時）。

Classes are held in the morning and afternoon, Monday to Friday, during the months of July and August. Every subject will be taught for 54 hours, i.e. 15 times for 7.5 weeks per summer. 

 

Ｑ：報考資格為何？ / What are the admission requirements?

Ａ：在職英語教師或從事英語教學相關職業人士，且實際任教英文科年資累計滿一年以上。年資以任職日起計，算至報考當年7月31日止。

In-service English teachers or someone who works in the fields of English teachinng with at least one year of practical experience in English teaching. Years of experience are calculated based upon the start date of previous employment up to July 31 of the application year.

 

Ｑ：英語教學經歷相關證明影本所指為何？ / What does it mean by “proof of English teaching experience”?

Ａ：自任職日起計，曾任教過的單位之年資證明（或離職證明上註明服務年資亦可）。

Proof of years of experience, which is calculated from the date of employment (or indicateyears of service on the termination of employment report)

 

Ｑ：何謂英語進修經歷相關證明影本？ / What does it mean by “documented proof of advanced level education in English”?

Ａ：舉凡參加過任何與英語教學/研究相關之課程或研討會，均請提供證明、證書或學分認證等資料。

Individuals who have attended classes or seminars related to English teaching or research should show proof of attendance, certificate(s) or credentials received.

 

Ｑ：請問「進修計畫」之內容及形式為何？是否可超過三頁？ / What is the standard format/content for writing the study plan? Can it be more than three

Ａ：內容：英語教學心得及未來研究方向，以英文撰寫。

　　形式：Ａ４紙張，12-14號字體，行距為double space。請儘量勿超過三頁。

Content: Your opinion about teaching English and future research objectives, written in English Format: A4 paper, 12-14 font size, double-spaced. No more than three pages.

 

Ｑ：請問何謂有利申請之英語教學/研究資料？ / What are those “supporting documents related to English teaching/research”?

Ａ：如曾自行發展獲得獎勵的課程規劃、或教材、學習單、評量等設計、教學觀摩影帶、教學成果展示等、與行動研究或進修的相關論述、指導學生比賽得獎等相關資料。因人而異，請自行發揮。

Individuals who have been awarded for exceptional efforts and contributions in improving teaching techniques and developing teaching materials.  Determination of “supporting documents” will vary from person to person.  Various documents may be submitted at the discretion of the applicant concerned.

 

Ｑ：報名文件如何提供給系所? / How to provide the application documents to the department?

Ａ：現已改採線上報名與線上上傳文件，請至政大招生專區的報名系統完成相關報名及文件上傳，上傳文件有大小限制，請依報名系統說明及規範。

The application is now changed to on-line application. Please upload the documents at the on-line application system. Plese refer to the on-line application system for the instruction and the file size limit.

 

Ｑ：需要在職證明嗎？ / Is “proof of employment” required?

Ａ：[「](https://etma.nccu.edu.tw/images/data/admissions/%E6%9C%8D%E5%8B%99%E6%A9%9F%E9%97%9C%E5%90%8C%E6%84%8F%E9%80%B2%E4%BF%AE%E8%AD%89%E6%98%8E%E6%9B%B8.doc)[服務機關同意進修證明書](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ghSEETqC25_3N9xTKnuom7OqepycjXkm/view?usp=sharing)」即可視為在職證明。

An authorization letter signed by current employer is equivalent to proof of employment.

 

Ｑ：[「教學經歷審核表」](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1GUpebE3U_WGfADPIeMytnfEW54kmEufC/view?usp=sharing)上的教學經歷或進修經歷欄如不敷使用，怎麼辦？ / What should I do if I need more space to write on the “Teaching Experience Evaluation Form”? 

Ａ：如不敷使用，請自行增加欄位。

You may add columns on the form on your own.

 

Ｑ：如果我想參考歷年考古題，要去哪裡找考古題? / Where to find the written exam questions for the previous years? 

Ａ：可至圖書館的「[各類考試歷屆試題](http://vms.lib.nccu.edu.tw/past_exam/)」查詢，級別請選「碩士在職專班」，學院請選「外國語文學院」，按下查詢後就會出現「英國語文學系英語教學碩士在職專班（ETMA）」選項，網站上僅提供試題，不提供解答。

You may refer to the [Written Exam Section](http://vms.lib.nccu.edu.tw/past_exam/index.php) under the NCCU library website for it. Only the question is provided. The answer is not provided.

2023 政大語料庫研習營

 

＃語料庫：掌握語言觀察密技！

 疫情解封後，迎來了期待已久的暑假！

讓我們一同探索令人著迷的語言學研究方法，深入瞭解可能的職業發展機會。

無論你是語言學新手還是經驗豐富的研究者，這裡都有適合你的知識和挑戰。

 

讓華語、英語和語料庫成為你的夥伴，

探索各種語言現象，解密其背後的規則和模式，

你將發現語言的無限魅力和豐富多彩的表達方式！

 這將是一次輕鬆愉快的交流體驗，

無論你是初次接觸語言學還是語料庫，

都能從中逐漸探索語言學的研究領域與發展趨勢。

需要提前報名（限30人），趕快預留你的名額吧！

 讓我們一同開啟這段令人興奮的語言學之旅！

本英語教學碩士在職專班研究生修滿18學分後，始得修習「論文指導」，於修習該課程時需提出論文/專業實務報告計畫書審查之申請。

論文/專業實務報告計畫書審查委員由系主任聘請校內或校外一位老師與指導教授共同擔任之。

論文計畫書需以英文書寫，以10至15頁為限。其內容應包括：

研究探討之問題

相關文獻

研究方法

主要內容

預期結果

參考文獻

專業實務報告計畫書需以英文書寫，以10至15頁為限。其內容應包括 :

專業實務成果理念與個案描述(實務案件之背景與希望達成之目標與目的、實務施作之場域與對象)

學理基礎(與施行案件相關之專業知識背景、文獻資料整理說明)

方法技巧詮釋及分析(施作方法工具、分析方式方法與步驟)

成果貢獻及其他衍生性成就(實務案件之成果呈現、實務施作成果之衍伸討論與文獻比對、實務建議與結語)

論文/專業實務報告計畫書審查要點：

計畫書中之基本審核要項： 

(1)寫作(quality of writing)

(2)研究方法與理論/實務之運用(application of theory, method, and practice)

(3)論文/專業實務報告組織與範圍(organization and scope of the thesis/professional practice report)

 審查委員在審查後提出書面評語、經由指導教授轉予學生參考。

6. 論文/專業實務報告計畫書審查成績分「通過」及「不通過」，通過標準以七十分為及格。兩位委員的分數皆須為七十分（含）以上，方屬通過。如兩位委員中有一位評為通過，另一位評為不通過，則送第三位計畫書審查委員。三位委員中需有兩人（含）以上認定通過方為通過。若審核未通過，修改後可重新申請審核。

7. 其他未盡事宜，應由「英語教學碩士在職專班」班務會議議決之。

8. 本辦法經系務會議通過後實施，修訂時亦同。

論文暨專業實務報告考試須知

 

92年8月5日ETMA班務會議修正通過

(部分條文經93.3.3行政電腦化推動小組畢業離校程序協商會議決議修改)

111年1月3日教務會議修訂通過

 

一、申報論文/專業實務報告題目

1.專班學生應撰寫論文，惟可依其需求提出申請以「專業實務報告」替代「論文」。

2.於修習「論文指導」時申報，且論文/專業實務報告題目須與系所專業相符。

3.請先登入iNCCU學生資訊系統申報論文題目，列印論文題目申報單送請指導教授確認後簽名，於系辦公室公告之日期前繳交，陳請系主任確認簽名。 （如需邀請校外老師擔任指導教授須另繳交一份「校外論文指導教授略歷表」且經班務會議通過。）

       4.題目已申報但需要更改者，可在每年三月或九月底重填一次申報單，並在申報單右上角以紅筆加註「更改題目」。 

二、申請學位考試

1.論文/專業實務報告考試申請截止日期明定於「國立政治大學研究生學位考試要點」中，申請書須於截止日前送達系辦，唯申請時須已通過論文/專業實務報告計畫書審查。

2.申請論文/專業實務報告考試時請檢具：

a.「研究生學位考試申請表」一份﹝填寫完畢後自行送請指導教授簽名﹞。

b. 完稿論文三冊。

3.指導教授提四至五名學位考試委員（至少一名須為校外老師），再由主任勾選最後三名學位考試委員。

三、撰寫須知

 1.論文撰寫須知：論文摘要應依研究目的、文獻、研究方法、研究內容及研究結果等摘要撰寫。論文須依照本碩士在職專班「碩士論文格式」撰寫，格式不符者不得申請學位考試。

2.專業實務報告撰寫須知：專業實務報告須依照本碩士在職專班「碩士論文格式」撰寫，格式不符者不得申請學位考試。專業實務報告頁數約30至50頁，內容應包含專業實務成果理念與個案描述(實務案件之背景與希望達成之目標與目的、實務施作之場域與對象)、學理基礎(與施行案件相關之專業知識背景、文獻資料整理說明)、方法技巧詮釋及分析(施作方法工具、分析方式方法與步驟)、成果貢獻及其他衍生性成就(實務案件之成果呈現、實務施作成果之衍伸討論與文獻比對、實務建議與結語)等。

四、論文/專業實務報告考試

1.申請手續完成後三至六週舉行考試。

2.學位考試結束後，研究生須依學位考試委員意見修改論文，並經系主任及指導教授複審通過後方可付印。

五、 線上建檔、繳交論文/專業實務報告與離校手續

1.辦理離校手續前，須完成「政大博碩士論文線上建檔」。

2.繳交論文/專業實務報告二本平裝至系辦公室並依圖書館規定辦理繳交。

3.通過學位考試者，須上網檢核個人所需辦理之離校程序後列印「離校程序單」，再憑單至系辦及各承辦單位辦理離校手續。

六、本辦法經ETMA班務會議通過後實施，修訂時亦同。本辦法未盡事宜，依本校相關規定辦理。

8.余明忠老師之「英文字彙教學」，從7/7 ~ 8/25止，皆在井塘020110教室上課。上課時間每週二四下午13:30 ~16:40。

title: Studies on English Teaching Methods.pdf
text:
Studies on English Teaching Methods
& Material Evaluation
(Summer, 2008 ETMA Program)
by Prof. Po-ying Lin
Course Description
This course deals with discussions of and research into various topics of current interest
to TESL/TEFL learners. It will emphasize new approaches to problems facing the field and
the development of understanding methods as well as study of materials leading possible
solutions.
Course Objectives
This course aims to
1. provide the theoretic background of ESL/EFL learning.
2. provide an overview of the major types of English teaching methods.
3. introduce the latest development in English teaching.
4. provide strategies for the teaching of four English skills—listening, speaking, reading,
& writing, and the teaching of vocabulary, grammar and discourse.
5. provide the guideline for syllabus design and material evaluation.
6. provide the concepts of learning autonomy.
7. provide techniques for classroom-based assessment and computer assisted language
learning (CALL).
8. equip the learner with the ability to formulate a teaching method and related classroom
activities appropriate for the particular teaching task he/she is supposed to undertake.
9. arouse the learner’s interest to carry out a research project on his/her own.
Activities: lecture, oral presentation, discussion, video-viewing, and teaching demonstration.
Requirements & Grading
1. Regular attendance and active participation in class discussion. 20%
2. Oral presentation and teaching demonstration. 50%
3. A term paper of 6-10 pages in length (excluding bibliography and appendixes) on any
topic concerning EFL/ESL teaching. 30%
Textbook and Materials:
1. Celce-Murica, M. (2001 3rd ed.). Teaching English as a Second or Foreign Language.
Heinle & Heinle.
2. Selected readings from major references and other related articles.

尤雪瑛 副教授
Course description
This course is designed to familiarize students with the process involved in
writing a thesis proposal which will lead to the successful writing of the thesis at the
completion of this master’s program.
Requirements
1. Attend the beginning and final sections given by the instructor.
2. Consult with individual advisor regularly.
3. Give a 5-10 minute presentation on the proposal.
4. Submit a written thesis proposal one week after the presentation.
Grading
80% of the score will come from the results of the proposal review. (40 % each
by the individual thesis advisor and the other reviewer)
20% of the score will be given by the instructor on the performance of the
presentation.

title: Second Language Research Methods.pdf
text:
Second Language Research Methods
英語教學研究方法
Summer 2008
Prof. Ming-chung Yu
余明忠 教授
Course Description
The purpose of this course is to introduce a clear and comprehensive overview of
linguistic research methods in applied linguistics. The course is aimed at those who
are new to studies in the field of language learning or who may have done or written
some research work without academic guidance. Specific focus is on how to help
education researchers and classroom teachers understand and critique published
studies in applied linguistics. After completing this course, students are expected to
have become interested enough to delve further into the literature and maybe even to
embark on research of their own.
Required Course Books
Nunan, David. Research Methods in Language Learning, 10th printing. Cambridge
University Press, 2001.
Brown, H. Douglas, and Susan Gonzo. Readings on Second Language Acquisition.
London: Prentice Hall, 1995.
Course Requirements
Grade for the course will be computed as follows: (i) exam: 60%, (ii) oral
presentation: 20%, and (iii) class participation: 20%

Studies on Course Design and Material Evaluation
By P. Y. Lin & S. F. Su
Summer, 2008 Tue. 1:30-4:40 p.m. & Fri. 9:00-12:10 a.m.
Course Description:
This course aims to provide students with the major approaches of language
syllabus/curriculum/course design and the guidelines for analyzing, evaluating, and
developing EFL materials. Students are to survey and compare different English
language syllabus/curriculum/course designs and various kinds of English teaching
materials used in Taiwan and some other Asian countries, so as to equip them with the
ability to design a language program/language course and enable them to select, adapt
and hopefully, write teaching materials for EFL courses as well.
Activities:
Lecture; oral presentation; discussion; survey; design of /evaluation on different English
language syllabus/curriculum/course and teaching materials.
Requirement & Grading:
A. S. F. Su: (Course Design)
1. Regular attendance and active participation in classroom discussion. (10%/20%)
2. Oral presentation as well as some critical comments on the papers or the issues
concerned. (20%/0%)
3. Group project on any of the following: (20%/30%) (Written work)
(1) Conduct a need survey with a particular group.
(2) Design a language program for a particular group of students (e.g. an adult
English program at YMCA).
(3) Evaluate a language program/a teacher training program.
(4) Make a critical comment on any article inside the reading materials.

Course description: This course covers two parts: the syntactic structures of English
that are crucial to learners of English, and how to teach this grammar. The
purpose is to provide students with knowledge of grammatical structures
required in teaching English to Chinese speakers. Students learn to develop
skills in grammatical analysis and then apply concepts and knowledge studied

title: Second Language Acquisition2014.pdf
text:
Second Language Acquisition
Instructor: Ming-chung Yu
Ph.D., Harvard University, 1999
Distinguished Professor of Applied Linguistics
Department of English
National Chengchi University
Course Description
This course is intended to provide an overview of linguistic research on second
language (L2) learning, such as language development in children and adults; the
acquisition of phonological, morphological, and syntactic systems; the role of both
parent and child in the acquisition of communicative competence. This course will
pay special attention to the most important issues of second language acquisition
(SLA). More importantly, this course will discuss the implications of research on L2
for foreign language learning. The course will thus explore the multiple aspects of this
area, including theoretical background; the nature of language learning, styles and
strategies, personality factors, sociocultural factors, communicative competence,
interlanguage, contrastive and error analysis, the learning of various language skills
(listening, speaking, reading, writing), and recent developments in all of these areas.
Reference Book
Brown, H. Douglas. Principles of Language Learning and Teaching (5th, ed).
London: Prentice Hall, 5th, ed., 2007 (main textbook).

text:
Discourse Analysis and English Teaching 1
Course Title Discourse Analysis and English Teaching Summer,2014
Course Code 951942001
Time Tue. 13:30-16:40 Thur. 9:00-12:10
Place 2 5 0 3 09
Instructor Hsueh-ying Yu
Course Description
This course is to introduce students to the study of discourse analysis and its
application to English teaching. A general review of discourse studies will be the
focus of the class in the first few weeks, which characterizes the nature of discourse
analysis and relationships between sentence structure and discourse grammar.
Follow-up topics on discourse analysis will cover coherence, discourse structure,
information distribution and topic continuity. Finally, traditional grammatical issues
concerning the use of conjunctions, subordination and tense-aspect will be
reexamined from the discourse perspective.

title: Fiction and English Teaching2014.pdf
text:
Fiction and English Teaching Dr. Chao-ming Chen
Summer 2014 Office: 02-27051275
Email: cmchen.en@gmail.com
Course Description:
This course aims at emphasizing the use of fiction or stories as a popular
technique for teaching language skills and reading strategies in Taiwan’s middle and
high schools, recognized as ESL or EFL programs. Literary and pedagogical theories
will be introduced to help instructors construct appropriate teaching modules for their
English classrooms. Instructors will be required to demonstrate their classroom
practices, sharing their achievements and frustrations in teaching English through
literature. The class will be also oriented to the discussion of possibilities and
potentials in developing new approaches of language teaching.

Course Overview
Teaching Reading and Writing in English is a graduate-level course that provides a broad
overview of various issues and strategies in teaching reading and writing in the context of
English as a Foreign Language.
Learning Objectives
By the end of the semester, you should be able to:
 Be familiar with various issues in teaching reading and writing in EFL context.
 Explain various approaches to reading and writing instruction
 Integrate the discussed instruction in a real-life course
 Provide effective feedback on student writing
 Design individual and group activities to facilitate writing and reading development
 Assess student reading and writing effectively to maximize literacy development

Course Policies
Late Submissions. You are expected to complete all assigned work on time. Late or
incomplete work will not be accepted, responded to, or evaluated.
Reading. You are expected to read all the assigned readings. In addition, you are expected to
do extra readings on the topic of your choice to complete your final project.
Feedback. You are encouraged to make an appointment with me if you wish to receive
feedback on any aspect of your work throughout the semester. Ongoing feedback will be
provided in class, but if you would like to receive feedback on your written work, make an
appointment. Before discussing your written work by making an appointment, please provide
the following information: 1) Your own assessment of the project (e.g., what you are trying
to do; how you have accomplished the goals; how the project falls short of meeting your
goals; what you are struggling with); 2) a description of what you plan to do with the project
after receiving the feedback (e.g., revise into an applied project or thesis/dissertation proposal;
submit for publication); and 3) what kind of feedback you wish to receive.

You will be asked to write 6 reflections. Your entries can be your reflections on the reading,

You are required to design a reading/writing course, syllabus, materials, and activities.

This course aims to give English Teachers some experiences in teaching

Course Description
The purpose of this course is to introduce a clear and comprehensive overview of
linguistic research methods in applied linguistics. The course is aimed at those who

The objective for the speaking part of the course is for EFL teachers to
understand how they could design and use speaking tasks that will actually
improve students' speaking fluency and to explain the problems and successes

highly appraised for its integration of theory and practice, the class will

General Course Description：
The course will be devoted to the study of the structure of English words and the
forms of English words, including most common base forms and rules by which
alternate forms are derived. Lectures will consist of vocabulary teaching methods,
the background of English and sources of English vocabulary, changing meanings of
words, analysis of word structure, including inflection, derivation, and native and
borrowed word-formational processes. Students may expect to achieve substantial
enrichment of their vocabulary while learning about etymology and abstract rules of
English word formation.

The course is offered to English teachers who are interested in an innovative
teaching method—using Creative Drama and dramatic arts in all levels of English

and regularly finish all assigned presentations to get a passing grade. Some reading
materials will be discussed in class; others should be read outside class time. Details
of all assignments and reading preparations will be announced one week ahead. Three
absence, late appearance or late assignment will greatly affect the final grade. Good
team work is expected; therefore, group assignments should be accomplished among
different class members. Any suggestion to the instructor on teaching methods/due
dates will be seriously considered and students are encouraged to make negotiations at
the beginning of the course but not at the end.

title: Research Paper Writing2012.pdf
text:
Research Paper Writing
研究報告寫作
Summer 2012
Prof. Ming-chung Yu
余明忠 教授
I. Course objective
This course is intended to help students acquire the specific skills in writing a
thesis. With this objective in mind, the teacher will focus his instruction on two
aspects. First, he will teach students what to write in each chapter of the thesis, i.e.,
what should be included in each chapter. Second, he will teach them how to write,
including (1) the ways of organizing, summarizing, paraphrasing, and writing
critically; (2) the uses of verbal tenses in each chapter; and (3) the uses of APA format
in citation and references. Well equipped with the knowledge of what to write and
how to write, students will be able to write the thesis skillfully.
II. Course outline
The class will be conducted based on the organization of the thesis: (1) Chapter
One: Introduction; (2) Chapter Two: Review of Related Literature; (3) Chapter Three:
Method; (4) Chapter Four: Results; and (5) Chapter Five: Discussion. After all of
these, the abstract will be introduced and discussed.
III. Schedule
Unit 1: Introduction/Organization of the thesis

Session 2: Organization of the thesis

Also refer to the guidelines drawn up by English Department

Chapter Two due
Unit 7: Chapter Four: Results & Chapter Five: Discussion
Session 1: How to write Chapter Four: Results
WUR: pp. 136-159

Session 2: How to write Chapter Five: Discussion
WUR: pp. 160-183
Discussion of your Chapter Three draft
Unit 8: Abstract
Session 1: How to write an abstract
WUR: pp. 184-197
Chapter Three due
IV. Teaching method
Basically, the class will be conducted in the way of discussion. The discussion
is expected to function in two ways: (1) To clarify the difficult or confusing points
students encounter in learning the step-by-step procedure in each chapter; and (2) to
help students solve the problems they have in practicing writing their proposed topics.

In addition, the class will also be conducted in a friendly and pleasant atmosphere.
V. Course requirements and grading
Since the course is to help students acquire the necessary skills in writing the
ETMA thesis, the students are required to choose a research topic at the very
beginning of the class sessions to carry through the step-by-step procedure under the
instruction. Deadlines are set for the assignments of chapters one, two, and three.
Before the deadlines, prewriting and revision are greatly encouraged.
The grading system is based on students’ performance in writing chapter one
(20%), chapter two (35%), chapter three (30%), and other assignments for
reinforcement (15%).
VI. Textbook
Writing Up Research: Experimental Research Report Writing for
Students of English written by Robert Weissberg and Suzanne, 1990 (The book is a
straightforward and readable guide to the conventions English-speaking researchers
follow when they write up their work.).

title: Second Language Acquisition2012.pdf
text:
Second Language Acquisition
Instructor: Ming-chung Yu
Ph.D., Harvard University, 1999
Professor
Department of English
National Chengchi University
Course Description
This course is intended to provide an overview of linguistic research on second
language (L2) learning, such as language development in children and adults; the
acquisition of phonological, morphological, and syntactic systems; the role of both
parent and child in the acquisition of communicative competence. This course will
pay special attention to the most important issues of second language acquisition
(SLA). More importantly, this course will discuss the implications of research on L2
for foreign language learning. The course will thus explore the multiple aspects of this
area, including theoretical background, the nature of language learning, styles and
strategies, personality factors, sociocultural factors, communicative competence,
contrastive and error analysis, and recent developments in all of these areas.
Required Book
Brown, H. Douglas. Principles of Language Learning and Teaching, 5th ed. London:
Prentice Hall, 2007.
Course Grade
Class participation (15%); class presentation (35%); exams (50%)
Course Outline
Week 1: An overview of SLA; Age and acquisition I (Ch 3)
Week 2: Age and acquisition II (Ch 3); Language, learning and teaching (Ch 1)
Week 3: Communicative competence (Ch 8)
Week 4 Cross-linguistic influence and learner language (Ch 9)
Week 5: Class presentation: First language acquisition (Ch 2: pp. 25-48: from
Theories of first language acquisition to Discourse); Human learning I (Ch
4: pp. 87-110: from Pavlov’s classical behaviorism to Intelligence and
language learning); Mid-term exam

text:
Discourse Analysis and English Teaching
章法分析與英語教學
Summer 2012
Prof. Judy H. Y. Yu
尤雪瑛 副教授
Course Description:
This is an introductory course to the study of discourse analysis and its application
to English teaching. A general review of discourse studies will be the focus of the
class in the first few weeks, which characterizes the nature of discourse analysis and
relationships between sentence structure and discourse grammar. Follow-up topics on
discourse analysis will cover coherence, discourse structure, information distribution
and topic continuity. These topics serve as tools for text analysis and thus can be
integrated into the teaching of the four language skills, in particular, reading and
writing instructions. Finally, traditional grammatical issues concerning the use of
conjunctions, subordination and tense-aspect will be reexamined from the discourse
perspective.
Requirements:
Oral presentation, Written assignments, and Final report.
Textbook:
McCarthy, Michael. (1991). Discourse Analysis for Language Teachers. Cambridge:
Cambridge University Press.

text:
多媒體英語教學理論與實踐
Theory and Practice in Multimedia EFL Teaching
(ETMA, 2012)
Instructor: Chin-chi Chao, Ph.D. (with the invited facilitator, Professor Tsai, B. H.)
Time: 13:30-16:40 Monday & 9:00-12:00Wednesday, from July 4 to August 22, 2012
Classroom: Computer Lab 260509 at College of Commerce)
This course is about creating engaging language learning experiences with multimedia
for Teaching English as a Foreign Language (EFL) in Taiwan. The term “multimedia”
is used here simply because of general acceptance; we are fully aware of the fact that
“multi-media” is used more often to refer to the older generation of technology, while
“multiple media” or even “multi-modality” refers to more recent computer tools and
related phenomenon. Although integrated use of texts, pictures, photos, videos,
audio/sound, and various computer media has been taken as almost a norm when it
comes to creative language teaching in Taiwan, we have to ask to what extent such
English learning experience is actually better in the sense of more engaging and
meaningful for the learner. Particularly, in discussing multimedia in TESOL at this
time of technological development, we will put our focus on (1) the Web2.0 (social
media) and (2) mobile learning phenomena. We will explore how these newer forms
of multimedia tools have impact TESOL and how we could create and research
engaging language learning experience with these tools.

title: shakespeare-ELT-course_description-2018_e3967.pdf
text:
Course Title: Shakespeare and English Language Teaching, Summer 2018
Course Code: 951922001
Time: 9:00 a.m.-12:10 p.m., Mondays and Wednesdays
Place: Research Building, Room 250305
Instructor: Tom Sellari
Course Description:
This goals of this course all involve giving working teachers an opportunity to investigate the methods
and difficulties of using Shakespeare's works—and, by extension, the works of other major authors—in
their English language courses. Specifically, these goals include:
 familiarizing teachers with relevant literary and historical background to Shakespeare's works
 familiarizing teachers with resources such as dictionaries, reference works, films and videos,
and web sites for future reference
 gaining detailed knowledge of several of Shakespeare's works that would be of especially
interest to maturing students
 developing the reading and writing skills necessary to classroom flexibility and confidence in
dealing with challenging texts
 identifying and overcoming textual difficulties
 practicing incorporating some of Shakespeare's works into existing curricula
 developing classroom activities based on Shakespeare's works
Requirements:
Students will be expected to read a selection of Shakespeare's sonnets and excerpts from seven of his
plays (specified below). Attendance is mandatory. Grades will be based on the following three writing
assignments, which can be completed in any order but must be handed in on the dates specified in the
final syllabus (to be handed out in the first class meeting):
 a creative work based on a model from one of Shakespeare's works covered in class
 a four- to five-page critical paper on linguistic or literary aspects of one of Shakespeare's works
covered in class
 a class plan that incorporates part of one of Shakespeare's works into a language curriculum
Materials/Textbooks:
Materials will be made available for students by the instructor.

Alternatively, students may choose to use some of the following editions of Shakespeare’s works:
Royal Shakespeare Company, William Shakespeare: Complete Works
The Norton Shakespeare
Arden, Oxford, or New Cambridge editions of individual plays
Tentative Schedule:
7/4: introduction to course; introduction to Shakespeare; Shakespeare’s sonnets; reference materials
7/9-7/11: A Midsummer Night’s Dream; comedy vs. tragedy; verse vs. prose; reading wholes
7/16-7/18: Othello; reading dialogue; pair work; writing dialogue; themes of race and prejudice
7/23-7/25: Twelfth Night; analyzing Shakespeare’s language; grammar and relations of ideas
7/30-8/1: Hamlet; rhetorical tropes and schemes; crafting and developing longer pieces
8/6-8/8: The Merchant of Venice; public speaking; argumentation and refutation; logic
8/13-8/15: Henry IV, Part One; history plays; definitions of history; reading motivations
8/20-8/22: Macbeth; review

title: Research Paper Writing.pdf
text:
Research Paper Writing
研究報告寫作
Summer 2009
Prof. Ming-chung Yu
余明忠 副教授
I. Course objective
This course is intended to help students acquire the specific skills in writing a
thesis. With this objective in mind, the teacher will focus his instruction on two
aspects. First, he will teach students what to write in each chapter of the thesis, i.e.,
what should be included in each chapter. Second, he will teach them how to write,
including (1) the ways of organizing, summarizing, paraphrasing, and writing
critically; (2) the uses of verbal tenses in each chapter; and (3) the uses of APA format
in citation and references. Well equipped with the knowledge of what to write and
how to write, students will be able to write the thesis skillfully.
II. Course outline
The class will be conducted based on the organization of the thesis: (1) Chapter
One: Introduction; (2) Chapter Two: Review of Related Literature; (3) Chapter Three:
Method; (4) Chapter Four: Results; and (5) Chapter Five: Discussion. After all of
these, the abstract will be introduced and discussed.
III. Schedule
Unit 1: Introduction/Organization of the thesis
Session 1: Introduction to the course
Session 2: Organization of the thesis
Writing Up Research (WUR): pp. 1-10
Unit 2: Chapter One: Introduction
Session 1: How to write Chapter One: Introduction
WUR: pp. 20-40 (five stages)
Also refer to the guidelines drawn up by English Department
and compare the two versions/also refer to the handout for the
guidelines further developed.
Consultation on your thesis topic
Session 2: Consultation on your thesis topic
Unit 3: Discussion of Chapter One draft
Session 1: Discussion of your Chapter One draft

Session 2: Discussion of your Chapter One draft
Unit 4: Chapter Two: Review of related literature
Session 1: How to write Chapter Two: Review of Related Literature
WUR: pp. 41-56
Chapter One due
Session 2: How to write Chapter Two: Review of Related Literature
WUR: pp. 57-72
Consultation on the outline of your literature review
Unit 5: Chapter Two: Review of related literature (continued)
Session 1: How to write Chapter Two: Review of Related Literature
WUR: pp. 73-89
Research questions and hypotheses
WUR: pp. 11-19
Consultation on the outline of your literature review
Session 2: Discussion of your Chapter Two draft
Unit 6: Chapter Three: Method
Session 1: How to write Chapter Three: Method
WUR: pp. 90-112
Discussion of your Chapter Two draft
Session 2: How to write Chapter Three: Method
WUR: pp. 113-135
Chapter Two due
Unit 7: Chapter Four: Results & Chapter Five: Discussion
Session 1: How to write Chapter Four: Results
WUR: pp. 136-159
Session 2: How to write Chapter Five: Discussion
WUR: pp. 160-183
Unit 8: Abstract
Session 1: How to write an abstract
WUR: pp. 184-197
IV. Teaching method
Basically, the class will be conducted in the way of discussion. The discussion
is expected to function in two ways: (1) To clarify the difficult or confusing points
students encounter in learning the step-by-step procedure in each chapter; and (2) to
help students solve the problems they have in practicing writing their proposed topics.
In addition, the class will also be conducted in a friendly and pleasant atmosphere.

V. Course requirements and grading
Since the course is to help students acquire the necessary skills in writing the
ETMA thesis, the students are required to choose a research topic at the very
beginning of the class sessions to carry through the step-by-step procedure under the
instruction. Deadlines are set for the assignments of chapters one, two, and three.
Before the deadlines, prewriting and revision are greatly encouraged.
The grading system is based on students’ performance in writing chapter one
(20%), chapter two (35%), chapter three (30%), and other assignments for
reinforcement (15%).
VI. Textbook
Writing Up Research: Experimental Research Report Writing for
Students of English written by Robert Weissberg and Suzanne, 1990 (The book is a
straightforward and readable guide to the conventions English-speaking researchers
follow when they write up their work.).
Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association (5th edition)
published by American Psychological Association, 2002.

This course aims to acquaint students with the theory of language testing and

text:
Instructor: Patricia C. Ssutu
Office: 745 Research Building phone ext. 88129
Office Hours: Tuesdays13-15, Thursdays 8-12, or by appointment
e-mail: cpssutu@nccu.edu.tw
Goals: Theatre In-Education is a special learning skill developed in Britain in 1960s
to join force of school systems and theatre groups for the purpose of teaching arts
and safely experiencing real life situations to high school students. It brings
theatre artists to schools to work with teachers and students to better understand
some human issues through relive historical events. The activities are highly
structured and materials carefully researched so that the outcome is closely
resembled to history but participants will have a better understanding of how the
decisions were made and what considerations were involved while making the
decisions. The TIE involves both theatre artists (actors/teachers) and audience
(students/participants). The students who take this course will learn the know-how
of TIE first and then, based on their own teaching experience, propose workable
strategies of TIE application in their own teaching environments.
Course Outline: The central theme for this year’s course is “Utopia: an
environmental friendly society”. Parts of outdoor campus (山頂公園) will be used
as the locale of the Utopia. Some projects will be executed there. The course is
divided into two parts: the first is the theories and techniques of TIE and the
second is the assessment of TIE incorporation into the school curriculum.
Teaching Style: This course is conducted entirely in English. The instructor will
function as a guiding force in motivating creative thinking and in building
learning and teaching materials. She will explain the rationale and the application
of each project. Students will be asked to work individually and/or in groups, to
participate in class activities and to find materials for projects and how to apply
them in their future teaching situation..
Assistant Job Description:
Keep attendance records
Keep assignment records and scores
Reserve and use video/audio equipped classrooms
Search for and make copies of teaching materials

by the instructor prior to class periods.

the reference section of the main library.

and NY: The Falmer Press, 1983.

jackson, tony. Learning through theatre: a new perspectives on theatre in

Theatre. Charlottesville, VA: New Plays Incorporated, 1987.
Mitchell, Ruth ed. Measuring up to the Challenge. New York, NY: ACA Books,
1994.
Schweitzer, Pam ed. Theatre-in-Education: Four Junior Programmes.
London:Eyre Methuen, 1980.
Course Requirements: This is an all-English class. No absence without reasonable
excuse will be permitted; more than three absences in the semester will suffer
severe grade deduction. There will be reading and writing assignments throughout
the semester and all assignments must be turned in on time. Group work is
essential for the course to work successfully; therefore, students are expected to
respect the kindred spirit and work cooperatively.

Summer 2009
Prof. Ming-chung Yu
余明忠 教授
Course Description
The purpose of this course is to introduce a clear and comprehensive overview of
linguistic research methods in applied linguistics. The course is aimed at those who
are new to studies in the field of language learning or who may have done or written
some research work without academic guidance. Specific focus is on how to help
education researchers and classroom teachers understand and critique published
studies in applied linguistics. After completing this course, students are expected to
have become interested enough to delve further into the literature and maybe even to
embark on research of their own.

Shakespeare and Language Teaching
instructor: Tom Sellari office: 季陶樓 340332
telephone: 2938-7249 e-mail: tsellari@nccu.edu.tw
Introduction:
This goals of this course all involve giving working teachers an opportunity to investigate
the methods and difficulties of using Shakespeare’s works—and, by extension, the works of
other major authors—in their English language courses. Specifically, these goals include:
•
familiarizing teachers with relevant literary and historical background to Shakespeare’s
works
•
familiarizing teachers with resources such as dictionaries, reference works, films and
videos, and web sites for future reference
•
gaining detailed knowledge of several of Shakespeare’s works that would be of especially
interest to maturing students
•
developing thereadingandwritingskillsnecessary toclassroomflexibility andconfidence
in dealing with challenging texts
•
identifying and overcoming textual difficulties
•
practicing incorporating some of Shakespeare’s works into existing curricula
•
developing classroom activities based on Shakespeare’s works
Grading and assignments:
Students will be expected to read a selection of Shakespeare’s sonnets and three of his plays
(specified below). Attendance is mandatory. Grades will be based on three writing assign-
ments, which can be completed in any order but must be handed in on the dates specified in
the syllabus below:
•
a creative work based on a model from one of Shakespeare’s works covered in class
•
a four- to five-page critical paper on literary aspects of one of Shakespeare’s works
covered in class
•
a class plan that incorporates part of one of Shakespeare’s works into a language cur-
riculum

II. Course outline
The class will be conducted based on the organization of the thesis: (1) Chapter
One: Introduction; (2) Chapter Two: Review of Related Literature; (3) Chapter Three:
Method; (4) Chapter Four: Results; and (5) Chapter Five: Discussion. After all of
these, the abstract will be introduced and discussed.
III. Schedule

IV. Teaching method
Basically, the class will be conducted in the way of discussion. The discussion
is expected to function in two ways: (1) To clarify the difficult or confusing points
students encounter in learning the step-by-step procedure in each chapter; and (2) to
help students solve the problems they have in practicing writing their proposed topics.

In addition, the class will also be conducted in a friendly and pleasant atmosphere.
V. Course requirements and grading
Since the course is to help students acquire the necessary skills in writing the
ETMA thesis, the students are required to choose a research topic at the very
beginning of the class sessions to carry through the step-by-step procedure under the
instruction. Deadlines are set for the assignments of chapters one, two, and three.
Before the deadlines, prewriting and revision are greatly encouraged.
The grading system is based on students’ performance in writing chapter one
(20%), chapter two (35%), chapter three (30%), and other assignments for
reinforcement (15%).

Students of English written by Robert Weissberg and Suzanne, 1990 (The book is a
straightforward and readable guide to the conventions English-speaking researchers
follow when they write up their work.).

title: Shakespeare and English Teaching course description2015.pdf
text:
Course Title: Shakespeare and English Teaching course description
Summer, 2015
Introduction:
This goals of this course all involve giving working teachers an opportunity to
investigate the methods and difficulties of using Shakespeare’s works—and, by
extension, the works of other major authors—in their English language courses.
Specifically, these goals include:
• familiarizing teachers with relevant literary and historical background to
Shakespeare’s works
• familiarizing teachers with resources such as dictionaries, reference works, films
and videos, and web sites for future reference
• gaining detailed knowledge of several of Shakespeare’s works that would be of
especially interest to maturing students
• developing the reading and writing skills necessary to classroom flexibility and
confidence in dealing with challenging texts
• identifying and overcoming textual difficulties
• practicing incorporating some of Shakespeare’s works into existing curricula
• developing classroom activities based on Shakespeare’s works
Grading and assignments:
Students will be expected to read a selection of Shakespeare’s sonnets and three of his
plays. Attendance is mandatory. Grades will be based on four writing assignments,
plus in-class activities:
• a creative work based on a model from one of Shakespeare’s works covered in class
• explanations of two short passages from Shakespeare and how they might be used
• a class plan that incorporates the two short passages from Shakespeare’s works into
a detailed class plan

title: Self Agency and Identity2015.pdf
text:
語言學習者的自我概念專題
Self, Agency and Identity in the Social Context of Language Learning & Teaching
ETMA 2015 Summer
一、前言與理念
語言教室裡最重要的人物應該就是語言學習者了。我們常聽到老師們習慣性
把學生分成有動機與沒動機兩種、覺得他們好被動，沒甚麼自主學習能力。但是,
站在學習者自我概念相關理念思考的話，就會知道這其實不是有與沒有的問題，
學生的動機也好，自主力也好，不可能是固定不變的，它跟學生所處的社會文化
場景有關，與學習者所認定的自我形象 (identity)是連動的。而自我形象的強弱
變化也常會引發學習者決定改變現狀，發揮出agency的表現。也就是說，學生
願不願意「投資」自己的精力時間，是有很多環境因素的，教室裡的互動其實也
沒那麼單純，不是有或沒有某些心理特性就可以了，更不是文法單字都搞定了，
就順理成章可以所學的外語與人說話、互動。
早期對學習者議題方面的研究著重於動機(motivation)、情緒 (所謂的
affective filter)、焦慮感 (anxiety)、自主力 (autonomy)等相關心理概念，採的是
比較斷面的思維與研究方法；不論是時間、歷史脈絡或社會文化場景都拒之於探
討範圍之外，不太把這些議題跟學習者所處的社會文化環境想成是連動的狀態、
也不考慮時間會帶來變化，更常忽略了屬於學習者經驗中的複雜現實層面。
1990年後期，衛考斯基社會文化理論開始發揮影響，才帶動的一股研究新
浪潮。最近二十年因為Bonny Norton, Claire Kramsch, Leo van Lier, Gary
Barkhuizen, David Block等諸多學者的研究與理論推廣，語言學習者自我概念方
面的研究變得非常暢旺。
但是國外的研究，例如Norton著名研究中的加拿大女性移民經驗，強調學
習者所遭遇到的角力關係(power)、社會階級(class)、人種(race)、性別(gender)等
等議題，表面上與國人所關心的英語教學議題是有距離的，一般老師讀者可能看
不出關連與真正的關鍵。
為了探索屬於國人的觀念連結，本課程指在帶領同學們進入這樣的新興研究
領域。由閱讀別人的研究出發，並藉著實際進行質性個案與敘事研究，探索台灣
如何在屬於我們的特殊歷史、社會、文化環境之下造就你我這樣的EFL學習者，
而隨著時間與社會的變化，又如何讓我們的學生願意投資自己學習英文或者引起
學生抗拒英語文、讓他們得以或者不能夠在各種不同的正式與非正式的學習情境
之下 (如教室vs. 出國留學、打工、網路遊戲) 學習與使用英語文。如果你覺得
聽起來有點複雜，那我要說，嗯，現實本來就是複雜的。別擔心，這正是這類研
究有趣的地方。
這門課的目標有三：(1) 藉著閱讀與進行相關研究讓你對自己、對學生的語
言學習真正有深刻的認識；(2) 你會知道從頭到尾如何進行與書寫一個敘事/質性
個案研究；(3) 你也會完成一個初步的研究計劃。願意的話，可以繼續發展成論
文。
1

二、課程大綱
本課程有四項主要內容，包括觀念性的、研究方法上的、學習文化的、與實
際研究案例，下面是各個層面的參考書籍舉例。由於學期時間有限，我們會由以
下書單挑選精華，讓同學們閱讀，目標是帶領同學們至少完成一個相關的論文計
劃書。
1. 觀念探討Conceptual discussions
Block, D. (2007). Second language identities. London: Continuum.
Norton, B. (2012). Identity and language learning: Extending the
conversation (2nd edition). Bristol: Multilingual Matters.
2. 研究方法Methodology
Lieblich, A., Tuval-Mashiach, R., Zilber, T. (1998). Narrative research:
Reading, analysis, and interpretation. Thousand Oaks: Sage.

Thousand Oaks, CA: Sage.
3. 學習文化情境Cultural Context

Cambridge University Press.
4. 實際研究案例Studies
Barkhuizen, G. (2013). (Ed.). Narrative research in applied linguistics.
Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
Kalaja, P., Menezes, V., Barcelos, A. M. (2008). (Eds.). Narratives of
learning and teaching EFL. New York: Palgrave MacMillan.

title: 106_Fiction_and_English_Teaching--course_description_60289.pdf
text:
Fiction and English Teaching
ETMA 2017 Course Description
Tom Sellari
This course aims to familiarize teachers with the conventions of fiction in English, its main genres,
and major British and North American authors, in order to give teachers confidence in their ability
to to integrate fiction into their English-teaching curricula. Beginning with the rationale for
imaginative literature set out in historically significant works such as Sir Philip Sidney’s “Apology
for Poesie” and Percy Bysshe Shelley’s “A Defence of Poetry,” the course will use selected works
of a wide range of authors (Richard Brautigan, Shirley Jackson, James Joyce, John Cheever,
William Faulkner, J.D. Salinger, Madison Smartt Bell, Paul Bowles, Joyce Carol Oates, Ray
Bradbury, Jeanette Winterson, Terry Pratchett, Flannery O’Connor, Raymond Carver, Donald
Barthelme, John Burdett, Ernest Hemingway, Jane Austen, and Ursula K. LeGuin; time permitting,
the course may also include translations of works by Jorge Luis Borges and Gabriel Garcia
Marquez as examples of the influence of literature from other languages) to develop and illustrate
means of adapting fiction into English language lessons. In keeping with recent research into the
psychology of learning, emphasis will be placed on inspiring both understanding and creativity.

title: SLA.pdf
text:
Second Language Acquisition
Course Description
This course is intended to provide an overview of linguistic research on second
language (L2) learning, such as language development in children and adults; the
acquisition of phonological, morphological, and syntactic systems; the role of both
parent and child in the acquisition of communicative competence. This course will
pay special attention to the most important issues of second language acquisition.
More importantly, this course will discuss the implications of research on L2 for
foreign language learning. The course will thus explore the multiple aspects of this
area, including theoretical background; the nature of language learning; styles and
strategies; personality factors; sociocultural factors; communicative competence;
interlanguage; contrastive and error analysis; the learning of various language skills
(listening, speaking, reading, writing); and recent developments in all of these areas.
Required Course Book
Brown, H. Douglas. Principles of Language Learning and Teaching, 5th Ed. London:
Prentice Hall, 2006.
References
Ellis, Rod. The Study of Second Language Acquisition, 2nd Ed. Oxford
University Press, 2008.
Ellis, Rod. Understanding Second Language Acquisition, 12th impression. Oxford
University Press, 1999.
Larsen-Freeman, Diana, & Long, Michael, H. An Introduction to Second
Language Acquisition Research, 9th impression. New York: Longman, 1997.
Brown, H. Douglas, & Gonzo, Susan. Readings on Second Language
Acquisition. London: Prentice-Hall, 1995.
Course Outline
Week 1: Overview of SLA; Popular ideas about language learning: facts and
opinions
Week 2: Current issues in SLA; Age and acquisition
Week 3: Cross-linguistic influence and learner language; Class presentation;
Week 4: Mid-term exam; Strategies & motivations
Week 5: First language acquisition: the role of L1
Week 6: Human learning & learning styles; Sociocultural factors; Personality factors
Week 7: Communicative competence; Theories of SLA; Class presentation;
Week 8: Final exam

text:
Course Design and Material Evaluation

Course Description:
In this course, the instructor will familiarize students with the basic principles, major
approaches, as well as past and recent developments of course and curriculum
design. A number of criteria/models on material selection, evaluation, and
adaptation will also be discussed. Students will read and reflect on important
concepts, discuss and share relevant teaching experiences with class members, and
apply the learnt knowledge in a simulated or real scenario where they collaboratively
design an EFL course and prepare the needed materials. In addition, it is hoped that
students will acquire the ability to conduct a small-scale empirical research on topics
related to the course. A few more recently published articles from top-tier journals
are therefore also included in the reading list, providing students with real examples
of how to identify meaningful research questions, perform critical literature review,
collect and analyze data, and draw conclusions based on research findings. An
individual research proposal is thus required of students to practice such research
abilities. Throughout the course, students are expected to participate actively in class
discussions to demonstrate understanding of materials read and critical thinking on
research topics.
Materials:
1. Richards, J. C. (2001). Curriculum Development in Language Teaching. Cambridge:
Cambridge University Press.
2. A reading packet with a collection of journal articles and book chapters
Requirements:
1. Attendance and participation: 10%
2. Summary and discussion of assigned readings: 25%
Students will take turns leading class discussions on assigned reading materials. In
order to make sure discussions are prepared beforehand, all discussion leaders
are required to present an outline or summary of the assigned reading, give a
15-minute oral presentation with visual aids, and propose 5~10 discussion
1

questions to elicit participation from other participants.
3. Group project on course design and material evaluation: 30%
In groups of about 3, students identify a specific learner population and relevant
course requirements, investigate contextual factors and conduct needs analysis,
survey and choose materials, then propose a syllabus with course objectives,
course outline, tentative schedule, requirements and grading scheme, plus a
sample unit with detailed lesson plan. A 1~2 page written plan and a 15-minute
oral report is due in the 8th class meeting, in the hope that the plan will invite
discussion and comments from other class members and that the group will
make necessary modifications before they proceed to plan the details. In the final
two class meetings, each group has about 30 minutes to present their final course
package and provide necessary justifications.
4. Individual Research Proposal: 35%
On the last class meeting day, each student is to submit a written research
proposal on a topic of his/her choice related to the course. The proposal will
include a list of 1~4 research questions, justification for the significance and
necessity of the RQs, an annotated bibliography of 10~20 entries in the reference
list, and the proposed research method (including data collection and analysis). A
10-minute oral report in the 10th class meeting is expected to help students plan
ahead, think more reflexively and critically, consider challenges from other class
members, and improve the quality of the final written proposal.

Thesis Writing
論文指導
Course description
This course is designed to familiarize students with the process involved in
writing a thesis proposal which will lead to the successful writing of the thesis at the
completion of this master’s program.
Requirements
1. Attend the beginning and final sections given by the instructor.
2. Consult with individual advisor regularly.
3. Give a 5-10 minute presentation on the proposal.
4. Submit a written thesis proposal one week after the presentation.
Grading
80% of the score will come from the results of the proposal review. (40 % each
by the individual thesis advisor and the other reviewer)
20% of the score will be given by the instructor on the performance of the
presentation.

Seminar on English Vocabulary Teaching and Learning
英語字彙教學
Summer 2010
Prof. Chien-ching Mo
莫建清 教授
General Course Description：
The course will be devoted to the study of the structure of English words and the
forms of English words, including most common base forms and rules by which
alternate forms are derived. Lectures will consist of vocabulary teaching methods,
the history of English and sources of English vocabulary, changing meanings of
words, analysis of word structure, including inflection, derivation, and native and
borrowed word-formational processes. Students may expect to achieve substantial
enrichment of their vocabulary while learning about etymology and abstract rules of
English word formation.
Textbooks:
a. Stockwell, Robert and Donka Minkova. 2001. English Words: History and
Structure. Cambridge: Cambridge Univ. Press.
b. Sloat, Clarence and Sharon Taylor. 1996. The Structure of English Words. Iowa:
Kendall
c. Mo, Chien-ching. 2005. A Phonetic Perspective on English Vocabulary Teaching
and Learning. Taipei: San Min.
Grading based on：
a. Written assignment: word analysis 20%
b. Mid-term 30%
c. Final exam 50%
※The final exam will reflect both lectures and readings. Failure to hand in
assignments will lower the final grade.
